name: US inflation
summary: US CPI at 4.0%, pushed up by the oil shock
state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7% in August, as energy prices fed through, within the 3–4.5% Watch band. The Fed raised rates in September and held on 28 Oct, with markets pricing another hike in December. October CPI is due mid-November.
for_you: Higher US inflation keeps global interest rates elevated, which affects borrowing costs well beyond the US.
rubric_hit: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.

sources.title: FRED — CPI for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL)

why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
